DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 77 s. 2022 04 2022 MS. VICTORIA M. RODRIGUEZ Sole Heir, Mediatrix Hermogenes Rodriguez Estate gregorioenriquez@yahoo.com Dear Ms. Rodriguez: This has reference to your letter dated 03 June 2022 wherein you are seeking for guidance regarding the effect of a tax sale, particularly, whether an owner must be compensated of its price / tax due difference, in relation to an information received by your legal team from the local government unit that the latter has foreclosed a property due to non-payment of real estate taxes. It appears that the issue subject of your request falls squarely under the mandate and technical expertise of Department of Finance — Bureau of Local Government Finance (DoF-BLGF). Hence, we advise you to seek the DoF-BLGF's final position on the matter. For your guidance, however, may we state the basic rules on the foreclosure of properties due to non-payment of real estate taxes under RA 7160 or the Local Government Code of 1991 (LGC), which the Department is mandated to interpret. The power of local governments to levy and collect real property taxes is derived from Section 232 of the LGC. Owners of real properties who fail to pay the real property taxes levied on their property may have their properties levied upon and sold to pay for the real property taxes due thereon, provided that the mandatory legal requirements, such as notice and advertisement, are complied with by the local government unit (LOU). Accordingly, as provided under Section 258 of the LGC, when the real property tax and any other tax levied under the LGC, becomes delinquent upon the expiration of the one (I) year period from the time the tax becomes due and demandable, LGU concerned, may avail of remedies by administrative or judicial action. The administrative remedies available which are summary in nature are: (1) levy on real property; and (2) sale of real property at public auction. While the judicial remedy is availed of in the court of appropriate jurisdiction. Moreover, the remedies are cumulative, simultaneous and unconditional, which mean that any or all of them or a combination thereof may be resorted to and the use of one remedy shall not be a bar against the institution of the other. "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

Under Section 260 of the LGC, within thirty (30) days after service of the warrant of levy, the local treasurer shall proceed to publicly advertise for sale or auction the property or a usable portion thereof as may be necessary to satisfy the tax delinquency and expenses of sale. As to the auction sale, if no payment has been made, the delinquent property shall be auctioned at the appointed date, time and place. The property shall be sold to the highest cash bidder whose bid is sufficient to pay the delinquent real property tax, the accrued interest, and the costs of the sale, the total of which shall be the price for accepting any bid. Note however that, proceeds of the sale in excess of the delinquent tax, the interest due thereon, and the-expenses of sale shall be remitted to the owner of the real property or person having legal interest therein. Moreover, under Section 263 of the LGC, in case that there is no bidder for the real propeny advertised for sale, or where the highest bid is for an amount insufficient to pay the real property tax and the related interest and costs of sale, the Local Treasurer conducting the sale shall purchase the property in behalf of the LGU concerned to satisfy the claim and within two (2) days thereafter shall make a report of his proceedings which shall be reflected upon the records of his office. Relatedly, under Section 264 of the LGC, the sanggunian concerned may, by ordinance duly approved, and upon notice of not less than twenty (20) days, sell and dispose of the real property acquired under the preceding section at public auction. The proceeds of the sale shall accrue to the general fund of the local government unit concerned. Note that levy may be repeated if necessary until the full amount due, including all expenses, is collected. On the other hand, local government unit concerned may enforce the collection of the basic real property tax or any other tax levied under this Title by civil action in any court of competent jurisdiction. The civil action shall be filed by the local treasurer within the period prescribed in the LGC. In viéw of the foregoing, the price of the property being sold at public auction or tax sale is not based on its market value but through the highest bidder whose bid is sufficient to pay the delinquent real property tax, the accrued interest, and the costs of the sale. In this regard, the remedy of the owner of the delinquent property or person having legal interest therein is through redemption of the property sold under Section 261 of the LGC, wherein within one (1) year from the date of sale, shall have the right to redeem the property upon payment to the local treasurer of the amount of the delinquent tax, including the interest due thereon, and the expenses of sale from the date of delinquency to the date of sale, plus interest of not more than two percent (2%) per month on the purchase price from the date of sale to the date of redemption. Such payment shall invalidate the certificate of sale issued to the purchaser and the owner of the delinquent real property or person having legal interest therein shall be entitled to a certificate of redemption which shall be issued by the local treasurer or his deputy. From the date of sale until the expiration of the period of redemption, the delinquent real property shall remain in the possession ofthe owner or person having legal interest therein who shall be entitled to the income and other fruits thereof. Page 2 of 3

The local treasurer or his deputy, upon receipt from the purchaser of the certificate of sale, shall forthwith return to the latter the entire amount paid by him plus interest of not more than two percent (2%) per month. Thereafter, the property shall be free from the lien of such delinquent tax, interest due thereon and expenses of sale. However, as provided under Section 262 of the LGC, in case the owner or person having legal interest therein fails to redeem the delinquent property as provided herein, the local treasurer shall execute a deed conveying to the purchaser said property, free from lien of the delinquent tax, interest due thereon and expenses of sale. The deed shall briefly state the proceedings upon which the validity of the sale rests. We hope to have assisted you on the matter. Very truly yours, By the Authority of the Secretary: INGAN Unders etary for Local Government OUSLG/MLl/LLLS-LRALLD/rjki/clp Page 3 of 3
